reason: The React Trajectory tab becomes a server-rendered page of its own, built from the session log by a pure fold on the host: closed steps are fetched by cursor in step-aligned pages, the open step is a state region, and the overview is server-rendered SVG. The package's host half (live raw tool values) becomes the values component with count and byte bounds. Client virtualisation and pointer gestures are not built.

The Subagents section, breadcrumb switcher and the at-sign source are redrawn on the host from area A12's tree ledger in one bounded read, with every stop reason shown and owner-only interrupt and dismiss routes. The client catalog cache, per-level discovery and the sidebar resource type are not built.

The chat node for a workflow run becomes a transcript node kind registered with area C4's node registry over the four workflow session events, plus a detail fragment that shows limits, sandbox facts, the script, endings and live narration, which upstream left out.

The Background jobs section becomes the server-rendered views that area A19's job routes and its two stream interests draw, with chunks tinted by channel and a confirm form in place of the timed two-press stop. The client-only Clear is dropped because the registry bounds settled records.

The Shared tasks section and the teamwork switch are rendered on the host from area A12's task board fold and updated as a state region. The confirmation before switching teamwork off is kept; owner forms to create, reassign, complete and delete a task are added because the board accepts an owner principal as actor.

The changed-files card, review tab, delivery cards and file links become transcript nodes and routes drawn from the logged workspace/changes and deliverables/presented events and the stored hunks, so they survive a restart. Native opening in a host desktop application is replaced by browser preview and one download route that requires the logged event to name the file.

The Automation tasks page, editor, records and session clock marks become server-rendered pages over area A13's schedule service. The browser copy of the recurrence evaluator and the browser's zone list are replaced by a host preview route that validates as the user types and lists the next occurrences with clock-change notes; a save stays compare-and-set.

The preset picker, roster with default and read-only configuration viewer are rendered on the host over area A27's preset service. The viewer shows each child with the layer that supplied it instead of YAML text; the roster is no longer filtered by the Coding Tools setting; the analytics event becomes one opt-in usage event.

The one field maxResultsPerSession (default 1000, at least 1) is kept as values.Config.MaxResultsPerSession. Two byte bounds are added, MaxValueBytes and MaxBytesPerSession, because a count bound alone lets a thousand large values pin memory.

The web view still creates and edits no preset: the viewer is read-only. The damaging half of the bullet is removed elsewhere: area A27 edits a preset's children by nested layer operations, so an override no longer replaces the complete child list, and the viewer shows which layer supplied each child.
justification: Authoring a preset is editing composition, which has one owner and one validation path (layers, area A21 and A07's settings forms). A second editor in this view would be a second way to write layers. DH-ADR-UIWORK-8 records the choice.

reason: There is still no tree-wide message timeline. In the Go design a team has no mailbox: a message between agents is an ordinary logged user-role message with source agent-message in the recipient's session, shown there in the conversation and the trajectory with the sender's path.
justification: A timeline across a tree needs a query over several sessions by message source, which area A06's query does not offer, and area A12 defines a team as the tree plus a task board only. The messages are visible per member, one click from the tree.

reason: Narrowed. A person can now interrupt a running member and dismiss a settled one from the tree, and can reassign, release or delete a task. Starting and renaming a member are still not offered, and write scopes are still advisory and labelled so.
justification: Area A12's Start needs a creator agent and names are held by the ledger with no rename operation, so a person cannot start or rename a member without a new host operation. Enforced write scopes are listed by A12 as not designed.

reason: The limit exists because the desktop application serves pages from a dsh-app scheme that has no file route. There is no desktop application, so every page is HTTP and local images use area A19's session file routes on all pages.

The resolver adds the case upstream deferred: a token that is a suffix of exactly one recorded path, starting on a path-segment boundary, links. The candidate set is the turn's recorded files, so the match is cheap and still never guesses from the text; an ambiguous token stays inert.

The mention resolver takes its candidates from the workspace/changes event, which in area A08's design lists files a shell command created (labelled other) inside and outside a repository, so such a file links without present. A delivery card still needs present, because a deliverable is by definition a declaration.

Area A08's present records a digest and keeps a bounded copy in the blob store. The card says changed since presented or source missing and its download route serves the kept copy, so reopening or moving a session no longer depends on the source file.

Native opening is not part of this view: there is no desktop application. The actions that always exist are the browser's own, preview and download; opening a directory in a host application is area A18's optional openpath component and the card does not depend on it.

Half removed. The 5,000-line drawing cap is gone because hunks are paged by the host. Colour is still computed per hunk side, so a line inside a comment or string that starts above the hunk can be coloured wrongly; unknown file types stay plain.
justification: Only bounded hunks are stored with the event (area A08), which is what removed whole-file comparisons. Colouring with full context would need the whole old and new file again. The effect is cosmetic and limited to multi-line constructs.

reason: The review route renders only the bounded hunks area A08 stored for the event, never a file's complete text, and a file outside compareScope or above the bound is listed without content. The route declares the session as its resource and checks that the event belongs to it.

Narrowed. A file outside the workspace is still found only by the absolute path recorded at the time. What a person needs after a move no longer depends on that path: the comparison comes from stored hunks and a presented file from its kept copy; only opening the current file reports source missing.
justification: A path outside the workspace has no root to be relative to, so nothing can relocate it after the workspace or the viewing session changed. The card states the condition instead of failing silently.

reason: Area A19's job output route delivers chunks labelled by channel, and the output panel view gives standard error its own class, so the two channels are told apart. Order across channels stays approximate, which area A19 records on its own unit.

A delivery row in area A13's table carries a state (enqueued, ran, discarded, skipped, failed), the turn that claimed it and the prompt that was sent. The records view draws each state distinctly and links ran to its turn, whose ending the transcript shows. Rows of a deleted schedule are still deleted with it, by the user's own action.

History stays bounded by days and records on purpose (anything that grows with history is bounded) and the page says so. The byte gap is closed: a prompt is at most maxPromptBytes, so a records page is bounded by RecordsPage times that value, and each record is drawn as a preview whose full prompt is fetched when opened.

A delivery row names its message id and turn, so the record links to a window around that turn in the conversation instead of the session's tail. Deleting a schedule removes its still-queued message when this process holds the session, and the answer says whether it was retracted.

The bullet asks the host to enforce access. Area A13 does: the model may schedule only for its own session, only in a turn a person started, within caps. This view adds what a person needs to check it: each row shows whether a person or the model wrote it and from which session, and every schedule route is owner-only.

The tree draws the latest run of each member with the stop reason area A12 records (completed, aborted, error, max-tokens, refusal, start-failed, interrupted) and its run id, so a failure no longer looks like an idle child. An owner can interrupt any running member from the tree, not only through a continuable child's composer.

There is no per-level client cache to prepare. The breadcrumb menu is the same host-rendered tree fragment, fetched when opened by pointer or keyboard alike, read from the ledger in one bounded request.

Discovery is not a sequence of client reads that one rejection can cut short. The tree is one read on the host; a failed read is an error panel with a retry, and after a reconnect the region is re-sent whole as a state baseline.

The section is drawn from the whole tree of the root, so a member with children shows them without anyone having opened its conversation first. The page size bounds the read, and deeper levels are part of the same nested list.

The cause was that display labels can repeat. The Go ledger holds a short name unique among one creator's children, and the path of names is unique in the tree. The at-sign source inserts that path, which is what the model's send_message accepts, so the reference identifies one member; it grants no authority by itself.

A tool-change record opens to one line per added and per removed tool, each with its schema as of that request, instead of a comma-separated list; a message with tool changes and other content shows both parts. The detail is a fetched fragment, so the length of the list costs nothing in the row.

An in-flight record shows its recorded start time and the elapsed time since it, labelled as elapsed and never as a duration, and the overview keeps a start tick. Selection is no longer local: the selected record, turn and filter are in the URL, and every record has a link that opens a window around it.
In area A11's design the workflow service is the only way to create a run and it writes the run record itself, whoever called it, so there is no run without a record for the node to draw.

The log now carries the missing fact. On resume the lease holder appends member endings with outcome unknown and a run end with stop reason interrupted, and a background run is a job that settles with host-exit. The node draws those and never shows a lost run as running.

A member row links to the child's stored session at any time. A session page needs no live agent in the Go design (area A19 reads it through the store), so a finished member opens read-only; a deleted child shows as missing.

The run detail shows what the run record holds: interpreter, limits, sandbox facts, the script from the hosting call's logged arguments, each member's outcome and usage, stop reason, cause, exit status and cleanup, with live narration. The control is the one that fits: cancel the turn for a foreground run, kill the job for a background one. Static topology does not exist because the host never parses a script.

title: Every work view is a read model of a named owner: it keeps nothing, draws the owner's own words, and says when it is behind, pending or unavailable
The trajectory is a page of its own, built from the log by a pure fold: closed steps are pulled by cursor, the open step is a state region, pages are step-aligned
The timing overview is server-rendered SVG with links; there is no island and no pointer gesture
Raw tool values are kept in memory for live sessions only, bounded by count and bytes, and never written anywhere
Nested work is one host-rendered tree from the ledger, with the owner's full outcome words, and a person stops work only through the owner's operation
A schedule is edited in a plain form that the host validates and previews with the evaluator that will fire it
Deliverables are drawn from logged facts and stored hunks; files are previewed and downloaded, not opened on the host; a link is made only for a recorded path
An agent preset is chosen for a blank session and inspected, not edited, in this view
A person can read, page, search and link into the step-by-step record of a session, live
The time and token cost of a session is visible at a glance
The typed value a tool returned can be inspected while its session is live
A person sees the tree of subagents with how each run ended, opens any member, and stops or dismisses one
A team's task board is visible beside the conversation, and its owner can switch teamwork and unblock a task
A workflow run is a node in the conversation with its members, its ending and its detail
Background jobs are listed with their output, and a person can stop one
The files a turn changed or presented are listed, compared, previewed and downloadable, also after a restart
A person creates, edits, pauses, runs and deletes schedules, and sees when each will next fire and what each delivery did
A person chooses the agent preset of a new session and can see what any agent preset contains
Golden trajectory records for fixture logs, and a page at any cut plus the rows after it equals the page at the later cut
Paging backwards and forwards yields every closed step exactly once, also with concurrent commits and concurrent pulls
The open-step region shows a start and no invented duration, is empty with no open step, and shows closers after a resume
Inspector bodies are escaped and paged, a tool-change record lists each tool, and a record link opens a window that contains it
Trajectory search and kind filters run on the host and return only matching records with a correct next cursor
Overview marks follow recorded timing, a running record is a tick, merging keeps total time, and the SVG carries no style or script
The totals strip equals the fold values and marks behind and pending snapshots
The live value store is bounded by count and bytes, keeps no failed call, clears with its agent and appends no event
The subagent tree is drawn from a fixture ledger with nesting, order, a distinct label per stop reason, missing and dismissed members and the page bound
Interrupt and dismiss are owner-only, refuse a child outside the tree, answer 409 without a live root or lease, and act once per request id
The at-sign source lists resident members by a path that is unique and resolves to the child
Task board order and markers, the confirmation before teamwork is switched off, and 409 with the current task on a stale revision
The workflow run node at every cut, its disclosure defaults, interrupted after closers, an escaped script and bounded narration
Job views order live rows first, tint chunks by channel, show the lossy notice, post the kill with a request id and vanish when no job is visible
Changed-files cards and paged comparisons are drawn from the event and its hunks, each row once in both layouts
The deliverable download serves only a regular file the logged event names, reports a changed or missing source and refuses another session's principal
A file mention links by exact path, basename or unique segment suffix, and stays text when ambiguous or unrecorded
The schedule form maps each guided kind to its timing kind, returns 422 with the values kept and 409 with the posted values and changed fields marked
The next-run preview across a gap and an overlap matches the schedule area's time rules and equals the occurrence a create stores
Schedule list, search and records render every delivery state, an unreadable store as an error, a missing firing host as a banner and an invalid row without a form
The preset roster and picker: order, a disabled broken declaration, selection on a blank session, 409 after the first turn, a viewer with provenance and no secret
Every work-view route declares access and refuses an unbound principal, every view has English and Chinese golden output, and a composition without the owner has neither route nor section
The team message timeline lists agent-to-agent messages of one tree in time order, and the view offers no start or rename
A behind value is drawn with its cut, a pending value as a placeholder and never as zero or empty, and a lease held elsewhere removes the controls
The trajectory of a real turn is complete, live and linkable
A person watches and stops a subagent, a background job and a workflow run
The schedule form previews, saves, fires and records
Deliverables survive a restart and say when a file changed
A preset is chosen for a blank session and locked by its first turn
